judged_text: With credential sharing enabled, `res` is the sync endpoint's fetch Response, so `res?.data` evaluates to undefined and `token.access_token` on the next line throws a TypeError, making every Google Calendar token refresh fail. Any deployment with APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED enabled gets a thrown TypeError instead of a refreshed Google token, so Google Calendar availability and booking flows fail once tokens expire.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then immediately uses `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch()` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), and `Response` does not have a `.data` property. That makes `token` undefined and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime, breaking Google Calendar token refresh whenever the sync endpoint path is taken.
